# SupportForge Gotchas

> Known SupportForge (remote endpoint agent) patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [&quot;Online&quot; agent at near-full disk is a heartbeat, not a working executor](online-flag-vs-hung-executor.md): a SupportForge agent at sub-1% free disk reports online but its executor is hung — one command completes per session, then "Session not found or has ended"; relieve disk out-of-band before remediating. HIGH.
- [execute_command can return another session's output when multiple agent connections are open](execute-command-cross-session-output.md): with 2+ concurrent agent connections, a correctly-targeted execute_command can silently return a different session's output; prefix every remote command with a hostname echo and verify it before trusting or acting on the result. HIGH.
- [Portal backend outpaces its UI — audit route payloads before scoping "missing" reports as backend work](portal-backend-outpaces-ui.md): the customer portal's endpoints often already return the data a "missing" report needs (fields, filters, pagination) — read the route/service payload before planning new endpoints, syncs, or migrations. MEDIUM.
- [get_ticket(N) resolves the internal id before the MSP number and can return a different client's ticket](get-ticket-id-vs-msp-number-collision.md): The URL number is an msp_ticket_number, but get_ticket resolves the internal id first; legacy Zendesk-imported rows have small ids in the same range, so get_ticket(195) silently returns another client's closed 2025 ticket. Resolve via list_tickets(search:"#N") then fetch by internal id, and assert organization_name matches before acting on an endpoint. HIGH.
- [list_tickets excludes closed but still returns solved, padding any open-work view](list-tickets-includes-solved.md): "closed are excluded" does not mean finished work is filtered out — solved is a separate terminal status that comes back by default, so an unfiltered queue silently mixes completed tickets into open work (45 rows vs 4 on the same query). Always pass an explicit status list. HIGH.
- [get_ticket_messages limit truncates from the oldest end, hiding the newest replies](get-ticket-messages-limit-truncates-oldest.md): messages are oldest-first and limit is a head cut, so lowering limit to dodge the oversized-payload error silently drops the most recent messages and inverts who-is-waiting-on-whom; keep the limit high and grep the saved payload for direction/stripped_text instead. HIGH.
- [Landing a local file on an endpoint via write_file: chunk it and verify](write-file-chunk-verify-transfer.md): write_file is the only inbound primitive and a single large base64 blob gets a char dropped/duplicated in reproduction (mod-4 failure, silent 0-byte file); split into ~2KB chunks with per-chunk SHA256 and a final md5 == source check. MEDIUM.
- [Ticket aggregates scoped by a single key (client_id or organization_id) silently undercount](single-key-ticket-aggregates-undercount.md): tickets are dual-keyed — native rows carry client_id ("org_..."), PSA-imported rows carry organization_id (prefix stripped) — so any report scoped by one key returns plausible-but-wrong counts (Reports said 1 created, Tickets said 12, same org/window); scope every aggregate with (client_id = $1 OR organization_id = $2) AND deleted_at IS NULL. HIGH.
- ["Launch was never delivered" is a stale command socket, not an offline machine](agent-stale-command-socket.md): connect_agent's two failure texts mean opposite things — "is offline" = unreachable, "launch was never delivered / no API instance holds this agent's command socket" = the machine is UP and only the socket is stale (commonly after an agent self-update). Restart the SupportForgeAgent service out-of-band via the RMM service-control endpoint; cross-check against a second agent to tell a slept machine from a stale socket. HIGH.
- [An organization's "users" count means recent requesters, not members](org-user-counts-are-recent-requesters.md): total_users on the organizations list and GET /organizations/:id/users both fold a one-year ticket EXISTS into what they call "users", so a 40-contact client reads as 12 — and the browse list applies the same default, so the count and the list agree with each other while both disagree with reality; return member_count and active_requester_count separately and carry `all=1` on any link to the users list. HIGH.
- [A technician session row marked 'active' is not evidence the session is live](active-session-row-is-not-a-live-session.md): nothing closes the row when the API process holding the agent's socket restarts, so every deploy leaves zombie rows (55 on one production API) that the launch flow hands to the browser as live session ids, surfacing as "Session not found" on every machine; a Redis owner record is no better because its 4h TTL outlives its writer — pair it with a short-TTL per-process heartbeat and reconcile before listen(). HIGH.
- [The dual-key org scope outlives the PSA that justified it, and then starts hiding rows](dual-key-scope-outlives-its-psa.md): the `(client_id = $1 OR organization_id = $2)` rule is right only while the PSA writes rows — after cutover it masks drift in the canonical key (a contact on a stale `client_id` still renders correctly because every display join ORs, while routing reads that key alone and filed 27 tickets against a non-customer), and any query that BRANCHES on the legacy key drops every contact created since (38 of 41 orgs). Collapse to the canonical key, but measure both-ways resolution first and backfill before deploying. HIGH.
- [A vendor with no per-tenant key in its payload cannot be fanned out over the org-mapping table](vendor-without-per-record-key-cannot-fan-out.md): integration_org_mappings works for Huntress/Pax8/QuickBooks/Meraki/Ubiquiti only because each vendor record carries an org id — Notion's /search returns one flat workspace with no per-record discriminator, so "fan it out like the others" writes the ENTIRE workspace to every mapped client and puts each customer's docs in every other customer's portal; reconstruct scope from structure (map a root page per client, walk each page's parent chain to the nearest mapped root) and write nothing for unmapped subtrees. HIGH.
- [A "Connected" badge that only proves a credential row exists hides a sync that has never run](connected-badge-hides-a-sync-that-never-ran.md): the card's green badge was a NOT NULL check and "Last updated" was the secret's save time, so Notion sat Connected for months while its scheduler filtered to client-scoped rows the UI never saved — every run reported a healthy "0 record(s) upserted"; record per-credential outcomes (last_sync_at/status/error/records) and render NULL as "Never synced", since a global task_runs table has no msp_id and looks correct only while one tenant is configured. HIGH.
- [`updated_at` on a credential row is not a sync timestamp when a code path rotates the stored secret](credential-updated-at-is-not-a-sync-timestamp.md): QuickBooks must persist Intuit's rotated refresh token on every test/sync, so updated_at means "a human saved this" for most services and "someone pressed Test" for QBO — any timestamp written by more than one code path is only as specific as its loosest writer; give the new event its own column and relabel the old one. MEDIUM.
- [A mounted API route still 404s from the dashboard until its BFF proxy handler exists](bff-has-no-catch-all-proxy.md): the dashboard is a per-endpoint Next.js BFF with no root catch-all, so an implemented, mounted, tested API route still answers Next's own 404 in the browser and never reaches the API — the API logs stay clean and every check at the API passes, which sends debugging to the wrong side (nav-counts left the sidebar counts silently absent for ~90 commits); curl the DASHBOARD host and read the body, JSON means the proxy exists and an HTML 404 means there is no handler. HIGH.
- [A client row with NULL msp_id silently drops every agent heartbeat on it](null-msp-id-client-drops-heartbeats.md): the shipped `generic`/`default` template clients leave msp_id NULL, and every tenant-scoped lookup compares `msp_id = $x` which NULL never matches — so a canonical-identity migration silently rejects each generic-installer agent at the first gate with a logless 400 (8 real endpoints unmanaged for 7 days while 440 scoped devices stayed healthy); never scope the shared template client (that funnels every MSP into one tenant), recover only from an explicit per-device assignment plus `reassignClientId`, and diagnose from the flatline split rather than agent logs. HIGH.
- [A dry-run copy of a migration left in database/migrations/ is applied for real on the next boot](migration-dryrun-copy-applied-on-boot.md): validating DDL against production inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` means stripping the migration's own BEGIN/COMMIT, and MigrationRunner picks up any `^\d+_.*\.sql$` that is not `_rollback.sql` — so a stripped copy saved beside the original is a second, untransacted migration, applied on the next deploy precisely while that version is still pending (the runner selects by high-water mark, not per file); write dry-run copies outside the repo and pick migration numbers from the working tree, not from schema_migrations. HIGH.

- [A tenant setting that is declared, rendered, and read by nothing](policy-key-declared-but-never-read.md): The policy registry builds the editor UI from a key declaration, so a key saves, versions and resolves in the chain with no consumer reading it -- the customer sets it, is told it took effect, and nothing acts on it. `serverConsent` shipped this way and every unattended session connected silently regardless of the setting. Grep every key for a reader before writing a section's first consumer, and never plumb a policy value through an optional argument a caller can forget. HIGH.
- [auditedRmmWrite flattens every throw but its own into a generic 500](audited-write-flattens-typed-errors.md): The wrapper maps only PrivilegedEffectRejected and PrivilegedAuditUnavailableError; a package's own typed refusal thrown inside the effect becomes INTERNAL_ERROR "Could not apply the change", so "this customer has turned off attended access" reaches the technician as a platform fault and gets escalated instead of fixed. Decide tenant gates before opening the audited transaction (also avoids holding the per-tenant advisory lock across slow work), and note the wrapper is staff-only — it calls requireRmmActor, so agent-facing routes must use withPrivilegedAudit directly. HIGH.
- [A capped list endpoint plus client-side matching is a record that vanishes past the cap](list-cap-client-side-match.md): `/v1/personas/list` clamps limit to 200 and orders by `persona_updated_at DESC`, so the person record and the org People tab -- which fetched a page and matched in the browser -- lost every one of 336 people past row 200: search finds them (server-side ILIKE over all rows) while the record it links to says "Person not found" and blames tenancy or a missing profile. Filter server-side (`user_id`/`email`/`client_id`), read counts from `total` rather than `items.length`, give a narrower fetch its own react-query key, and say "showing the first N of M" when a page is truncated. HIGH.
- [A migration numbered from the repo's highest filename is never applied and never warns](migration-number-below-deployed-high-water-mark.md): MigrationRunner only applies versions above the high-water mark in the deployed `schema_migrations`, and the highest filename on your branch is not that mark -- a branch cut before someone else's migrations landed sees a stale ceiling. Seen live: files stopped at 426 while production had applied through 435, so a `427_*.sql` would have merged, deployed and silently never run, surfacing as `relation does not exist` on production. Nothing catches it: the SQL is valid, git is happy, the suite never touches a database, and skipping is the runner's normal behaviour. Ask `SELECT max(version) FROM schema_migrations` against the deployed DB, then dry-run inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK -- `INSERT 0 0` on the migration's own ON CONFLICT insert is the collision, `INSERT 0 1` is a free number. HIGH.
- [A route module's `rmm-<nnn>-*` id is what the release gates read as "this package shipped"](route-module-id-is-release-gate-evidence.md): scripts/rmm-gates/delivery.js derives delivery by parsing module ids in src/routes/rmm.ts -- there is no ledger, so the number *is* the evidence and a plausible name can assert something false. Registering recording routes as `rmm-034a-agent-recordings` made GATE-04.5 report the native remote-desktop transport as delivered, a transport through which no session has ever been established; the failure surfaces as a harness rule ("GATE-04.5 is fully verifiable") that reads like a stale assertion rather than a naming mistake. An `rmm-027-*` id also commits the module to GATE-04.6: every one must write state inside auditedRmmWrite or withPrivilegedAudit, and device-certificate callers need the latter directly. HIGH.
